script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - MORNING

JAMES (30s, disheveled) sits hunched over a laptop on the outdoor patio. A STEREO plays classic rock in the background. James sips his coffee, glancing up at the cloudless sky.

JAMES
(muttering to himself)
10,000 hours... just need 2,000 more...

Waitress, LUCY (20s, bubbly), approaches with a notepad and pen.

LUCY
(smiling)
Your usual? And I heard you're a writer? My uncle's a screenwriter, it's so cool!

James rolls his eyes, slightly embarrassed.

JAMES
(sighs)
Yes, I'm a writer. But not quite the glamourous kind your uncle has.

Lucy places the coffee in front of him, her smile unwavering.

LUCY
You can't give up on your dreams, James. I've seen your work, it's really good!

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - LATER

James types away at his laptop, frustration building. He throws the laptop on the couch, stands up, and storms to the window.

JAMES
(to himself)
This isn't working! Maybe it's time for a career transition.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

James pours over books about screenwriting, marketing, and graphic design. He looks determined, but unsure.

JAMES
(murmurs)
Graphic design... I could do that.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

James meets with a local graphic designer, MARK (40s, professional). They discuss James' potential in the industry.

MARK
(smiling)
You have talent, James. And determination. I can teach you the rest.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James researches graphic design programs and applications. He sets up a makeshift workspace and begins creating his first design.

INT. BAR - EVENING

James meets with friends, explaining his decision to transition to graphic design. They're supportive, but skeptical.

FRIEND 1 (30s, cynical)
(laughs)
Graphic design? I thought you were a writer!

JAMES
(smiling)
Sometimes we have to adapt to new opportunities.

INT. MARK'S OFFICE - DAY

James interns under Mark, learning the ropes of graphic design. He struggles initially, but Mark's patience pays off.

MARK
(proudly)
You've got it, James. It's going to be a great career.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - MORNING

James, now more confident, sits at the same table as before. The stereo plays classic rock, but James is no longer lost in thought. He grabs a pen and notepad, ready to start his day.

JAMES
(whispers to himself)
I'm a graphic designer now. Let's make some art!

FADE OUT.

This modern screenplay follows the journey of James, a struggling writer, as he makes the decision to transition into a career in graphic design. Throughout the story, he faces skepticism from his friends and initial struggles in his new career, but with determination and the help of a mentor, he eventually finds success. This script showcases the themes of career transition and perseverance, all while maintaining a lighthearted, comedic tone.
